passage_text: Researchers investigated the effect of a novel antimicrobial peptide (AMP) on the growth of methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA) in vitro. The peptide was synthesized and purified to >95% purity. Cultures of MRSA were inoculated into tryptic soy broth and exposed to increasing concentrations of the peptide (0, 2, 4, 8, and 16 μg/mL). After 24 hours of incubation at 37 °C, bacterial viability was quantified by plating serial dilutions and counting colony-forming units (CFU). The experiment was performed in triplicate, and the mean CFU/mL was recorded for each concentration. A dose–response curve was generated to estimate the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) and the 50% inhibitory concentration (IC50). The data suggested a steep decline in CFU with concentrations above 4 μg/mL, indicating potent activity. Researchers also examined the peptide’s effect on biofilm formation by measuring crystal violet absorbance at 590 nm. The results showed a marked reduction in biofilm biomass at 8 μg/mL and higher. These findings support further development of the AMP as a potential therapeutic agent against MRSA infections.
stem: What is the CFU count at 8 μg/mL?
explanation: The table lists the CFU/mL at each concentration. At 8 μg/mL the CFU is 1.2 × 10⁶.
trap: Option B (4.8 × 10⁷) is the CFU at 4 μg/mL, not 8 μg/mL.

stem: Which control provides the baseline growth against which the effect of the peptide on CFU is judged?

options.A: MRSA incubated for 24 h at 37 °C in broth with no peptide (0 μg/mL)
options.B: MRSA exposed only to the highest peptide concentration, 16 μg/mL
options.C: Sterile broth with peptide but without bacteria
options.D: Heat-killed MRSA plated at each concentration

explanation: Correct: A. Untreated cultures grown under identical conditions give the baseline CFU (1.2 x 10⁸ per mL in the table) against which reductions are calculated. Why the others are wrong: B) A single treated condition has no untreated reference. C) Sterile broth with peptide checks for contamination but gives no bacterial growth to compare with. D) Heat-killed cells yield no colonies, so they cannot show baseline growth.
trap: Choosing a control that tests something else (sterility or killing) instead of the untreated growth baseline.

stem: Calculate the percent reduction in CFU from 0 to 16 μg/mL.
trap: Judging the drop by eye from 10⁸ to 10⁴ and guessing about 95%, instead of computing that only 3.0 × 10⁴ / 1.2 × 10⁸ = 0.025% of the untreated CFU remained (a 99.98% reduction).

stem: Which statement is NOT supported by the data?

options.A: CFU/mL decreased at each successive higher peptide concentration tested.
options.B: Biofilm absorbance at 8 μg/mL was 30% of the untreated value.
options.C: CFU/mL at 16 μg/mL was less than 0.1% of the untreated value.
options.D: The peptide eliminated all viable MRSA at 16 μg/mL.

explanation: Correct: D. The table lists 3.0 x 10⁴ CFU/mL at 16 μg/mL, so viable bacteria remained. Why the others are wrong: A) CFU falls 1.2e8, 9.5e7, 4.8e7, 1.2e6, 3.0e4, so A is supported. B) The table gives 0.30 against 1.00 untreated, so B is supported. C) 3.0e4/1.2e8 = 0.025%, which is below 0.1%, so C is supported.
trap: Reading a 99.98% reduction as complete killing.

stem: Which additional assay would best determine how quickly the peptide kills MRSA?
explanation: A time-kill curve measures CFU over time at a fixed concentration, showing the rate of killing and whether it is bactericidal.
trap: Option C (electron microscopy) visualizes damage but does not quantify killing kinetics.
